title: HDRTransDC High Dynamic Range Image Reconstruction with Transformer Deformation Convolution

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3, Dynamic Weight Fusion Block description immediately after Eq. (5)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper repeatedly claims that DWFB is spatially adaptive: it says the block will "spatially and adaptively select useful information across frames" and that the attention block senses exposure levels "in different areas." However, the next sentence states that the dynamic weight Δw is "shared in spatial dimension." A weight shared over spatial positions cannot assign different frame weights to different image areas, so it cannot implement the asserted spatially adaptive fusion. Either the statement that the weights are spatially shared is wrong, or the claimed per-pixel/per-area adaptive selection is wrong; the architecture must be clarified and corrected.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, Transformer Offset Estimator; implementation and dataset paragraphs in Section 3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: TOE is specified to use a learned absolute positional tensor "Pos ∈ R^{H × W × C}" added to the non-reference feature map. The stated training protocol uses randomly cropped 256 × 256 patches, while the stated dataset image resolution is 1000 × 1500 and the paper describes evaluation on those images. A learned tensor with fixed H and W cannot be directly added to both training-crop feature maps and full-resolution feature maps of different spatial sizes. The paper provides no positional-embedding interpolation, resizing, tiling, fixed-resolution inference, or alternative positional-encoding mechanism. As written, the described model has a dimensional incompatibility between its positional encoding and the stated training/evaluation image sizes.
